title: Build Array from Permutation
summary: Given a zero-based permutation nums, create an array ans where each element ans[i] is determined by nums[nums[i]], for all indices i from 0 to nums.length-1, and return ans.
statement: Given a zero-based permutation nums, create an array ans where each element ans[i] is determined by nums[nums[i]], for all indices i from 0 to nums.length-1, and return ans. A zero-based permutation is an array containing each integer from 0 to nums.length-1 exactly once.
constraints: nums is a permutation of 0 through len(nums)-1 with length at most 1000.
For every index i, output nums[nums[i]].
Do not reorder the input before following its indices.
reference_solution:
def build_array_from_permutation(nums):
    return [nums[value] for value in nums]
hints: Each permutation value is guaranteed to be a valid index.
For each value in original order, use it to index nums once more.
Collect those second-lookups in the answer.
The comprehension directly applies the required equation independently at every index, so it preserves order and produces every specified value.
editorial: The comprehension directly applies the required equation independently at every index, so it preserves order and produces every specified value.

tests.explanation: Following each value as a second index gives [0,1,2,4,5,3].
Each value points to the next value in the permutation cycle, giving [4,5,0,1,2,3].
